title: Iridium 33 and Cosmos 2251
summary: On 10 February 2009 an active Iridium communications satellite and a defunct Russian Cosmos satellite collided above northern Siberia — the first accidental hypervelocity collision between two intact satellites.
provenance_note: The archived February 2009 element sets for these two objects are held in Space-Track's gp_history archive, which this build could not reach. The orbits here are TLE-format element sets generated so that both objects' SGP4 tracks meet at the published time and altitude, over the published region, with the published inclinations and close to the published relative speed. Screening, closest-approach refinement and collision probability are then computed by the same code Kessler runs on the live catalog.
replay_hint: Run scripts/fetch_scenario_tles.py with Space-Track credentials to replay with archived TLEs.

event.significance: The first accidental hypervelocity collision between two intact satellites.
event.debris_label: Well over 2,000 cataloged debris fragments, many still in orbit.
event.source: NASA Orbital Debris Quarterly News, vol. 13, issue 2 (April 2009)
event.source_short: NASA Orbital Debris Quarterly News, April 2009

screening_window.note: Screening runs are replayed on an hourly cadence using only the element sets published before each run, with the live 72-hour look-ahead window.

sources.label: NASA Orbital Debris Quarterly News, vol. 13, issue 2 (April 2009): collision time, altitude, relative speed, inclinations and debris counts
Johnson, Krisko, Liou and Anz-Meador, NASA's new breakup model of EVOLVE 4.0, Advances in Space Research 28(9), 2001: the Standard Breakup Model behind the illustrative debris cloud
Kessler and Cour-Palais, Collision frequency of artificial satellites: the creation of a debris belt, Journal of Geophysical Research 83(A6), 1978

reconstruction.method: TLE-format element sets fitted so the SGP4 tracks of both objects pass through one encounter point at the published time and altitude, with the published inclinations. Generated by scripts/reconstruct_scenario.py.
choices: Encounter longitude 97.9 E is a point inside the published region (northern Siberia); the latitude is solved so the orbit planes cross at the published ~11.7 km/s relative speed.
Near-circular orbits (eccentricity 0.0002 and 0.0016) and zero drag terms are reconstruction choices, not archived values.
Element-set epochs on 7 February 2009 sit before the 72-hour screening window, as a real pre-event element set would.
